title: Men of Soul: The Eighties
theme: The svengali model carrying over from the prior decade — Maurice Starr built New Edition the way Rick James built the Mary Jane Girls — sitting alongside a family act (DeBarge), a visually distinct funk showman (Cameo), and the brief, hit-and-gone acts that defined the decade's middle (Ready for the World, Force MDs).
narrativePurpose: Trace 1980s male vocal group history through manufactured-group origins, label infrastructure, and film/soundtrack crossovers — keeping every personnel fact confined to active-career biography per series standard.
toneProgression: The hits and origin stories that defined the era → the lineup mechanics, labels, and city origins behind the sound → the archival pop-culture connections hiding inside this era's legacy

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-8-5 — the year Bobby Brown left New Edition, Ready for the World hit #1 with 'Oh Sheila,' DeBarge crossed over with 'Rhythm of the Night,' and Force MDs broke through with 'Tender Love.' The decade's middle, where most of this cast peaked at once.

rounds.name: RADIO HITS
rounds.description: The hits and origin stories that defined 1980s male vocal groups.

questions.question: New Edition's 1983 debut single, produced by Maurice Starr, reached #1 R&B and #1 on the UK singles chart. What was it?

metadata.fact: 'Candy Girl' (1983), produced by Maurice Starr, was New Edition's debut single — reaching #1 on the Billboard R&B chart, #46 on the Hot 100, and #1 on the UK singles chart.
metadata.storyHook: 'Candy Girl.' #1 R&B. #1 in the UK. New Edition's very first single — and it already topped two charts.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Candy Girl' (1983), produced by Maurice Starr, #1 R&B, #46 Hot 100, #1 UK. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candy_Girl_(New_Edition_song), Wikipedia (album) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candy_Girl_(album)

questions.question: Cameo, led by Larry Blackmon, scored their biggest hit in 1986 — #6 Hot 100, #1 R&B, UK Top 3 — with which single?

metadata.fact: 'Word Up!' (1986) was Cameo's biggest commercial hit — reaching #6 on the Hot 100, #1 on the R&B chart, and the UK Top 3 — a funk record distinctive enough to define the group's entire legacy.
metadata.storyHook: 'Word Up!' #6 pop, #1 R&B, Top 3 in the UK. Cameo's single biggest commercial moment.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Word Up!' (1986) #6 Hot 100, #1 R&B, UK Top 3. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_Up!

questions.question: The Whispers, produced by L.A. Reid and Babyface, scored their second and final R&B #1 in 1987 — also #7 Hot 100 — with which single?

metadata.fact: 'Rock Steady' (1987), produced by L.A. Reid and Babyface, reached #7 on the Hot 100 and was the Whispers' second and final #1 on the R&B chart — the commercial peak of a career that had already spanned two decades by that point.
metadata.storyHook: Produced by L.A. Reid and Babyface, years before they founded their own label. 'Rock Steady' was the Whispers' last trip to #1 R&B.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Rock Steady' (1987) produced by L.A. Reid/Babyface, #7 Hot 100, second and final R&B #1. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Steady_(The_Whispers_song)

questions.question: Ready for the World, from Flint, Michigan, scored a triple #1 in 1985 — Hot 100, R&B, and Dance charts simultaneously — with which single?

metadata.fact: 'Oh Sheila' (1985) reached #1 simultaneously on the Hot 100, the Hot Black Singles (R&B) chart, and the Dance chart — Ready for the World's only #1 hit, and a total commercial sweep for a single record.
metadata.storyHook: Three charts. One single. 'Oh Sheila' didn't just hit #1 — it hit #1 everywhere at once.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Oh Sheila' (1985) #1 Hot 100, Hot Black Singles, and Dance charts. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oh_Sheila

questions.question: DeBarge reached #3 on the Hot 100 and #1 R&B and Adult Contemporary in 1985 with which single, also featured in The Last Dragon?

metadata.fact: 'Rhythm of the Night' (1985) reached #3 on the Hot 100 and #1 on both the R&B and Adult Contemporary charts — DeBarge's biggest crossover hit, boosted by its prominent placement in The Last Dragon.
metadata.storyHook: #3 pop. #1 R&B and Adult Contemporary, at the same time. 'Rhythm of the Night' was DeBarge's furthest reach into the mainstream.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Rhythm of the Night' (1985) #3 Hot 100, #1 R&B and AC, featured in The Last Dragon. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_of_the_Night_(song)

questions.question: New Edition's 1984 follow-up, the first single from their self-titled second album, reached #4 Hot 100 and #1 R&B. What was it?

metadata.fact: 'Cool It Now' (1984), the first single from New Edition's self-titled second album, reached #4 on the Hot 100 and #1 on the R&B chart — confirming the group as a genuine commercial force rather than a one-hit act.
metadata.storyHook: #4 pop, #1 R&B. 'Cool It Now' proved 'Candy Girl' wasn't a fluke.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Cool It Now' (1984), first single from second album, #4 Hot 100, #1 R&B. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cool_It_Now

questions.question: New Edition was discovered at a 1982 talent show and co-produced for their own label by which Boston-based manager and producer?

metadata.fact: Maurice Starr discovered New Edition at a Boston talent show in 1982 and co-wrote and co-produced their 1983 debut album for his own label, Streetwise Records.
metadata.storyHook: A 1982 talent show in Boston. Maurice Starr saw something — and built an entire label around it the following year.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Maurice Starr discovered New Edition at a 1982 talent show, co-produced debut for his Streetwise Records. Source: Genius artist bio https://genius.com/artists/Maurice-starr

reserve.question: Force MDs scored a 1985 hit, written and produced by Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, that was also featured in the film Krush Groove. What was it?

metadata.fact: 'Tender Love' (1985), from Force MDs' second album Chillin', was written and produced by Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, appeared in and on the soundtrack of Krush Groove, and reached #10 on the Hot 100, #4 R&B, and #2 Adult Contemporary in 1986.
metadata.storyHook: Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis wrote it. Krush Groove featured it. 'Tender Love' became Force MDs' breakthrough on three different charts at once.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Tender Love' (1985, from Chillin') written/produced by Jimmy Jam/Terry Lewis, featured in Krush Groove, #10 Hot 100/#4 R&B/#2 AC in 1986. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tender_Love

reserve.question: Which DeBarge member served as the family group's primary lead vocalist on hits including 'All This Love,' 'Time Will Reveal,' and 'Rhythm of the Night'?

metadata.fact: El DeBarge served as DeBarge's primary lead vocalist on the group's biggest hits, including 'All This Love,' 'Time Will Reveal,' and 'Rhythm of the Night,' before launching a solo career.
metadata.storyHook: Every DeBarge hit you can name has the same lead voice: El DeBarge.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: El DeBarge was DeBarge's primary lead vocalist. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_DeBarge

reserve.question: Which New Edition member shared lead vocal duties with Bobby Brown early on, and remained the group's primary lead after Brown's departure?

metadata.fact: Ralph Tresvant shared lead vocal duties with Bobby Brown during New Edition's early run, and remained the group's primary lead vocalist after Brown's 1985 departure.
metadata.storyHook: Two leads at first — Tresvant and Brown. When Brown left, Tresvant carried the lead role forward on his own.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Ralph Tresvant was New Edition's lead singer, co-lead with Brown early on. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Tresvant

reserve.question: Cameo's Larry Blackmon became known for which distinctive visual signature, prominently seen in the 'Word Up!' video?
choices: A red codpiece and asymmetric high-top haircut

metadata.fact: Larry Blackmon's red codpiece and asymmetric high-top haircut, prominently visible in the 'Word Up!' video, became one of the most recognizable visual signatures in 1980s R&B and funk.
metadata.storyHook: You don't need to hear the music to know it's Larry Blackmon — the red codpiece and the haircut say it for him.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Larry Blackmon's red codpiece and asymmetric high-top haircut were his signature look. Source: Wikipedia (Word Up! imagery context) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_Up!

sources.title: Word Up! – Wikipedia (Larry Blackmon imagery in video)

rounds.description: The lineup mechanics, labels, and city origins behind the 1980s male vocal group sound.

questions.question: In which year was Bobby Brown voted out of New Edition over behavior issues, before launching a solo career?

metadata.fact: Bobby Brown was voted out of New Edition in 1985 over behavior issues, then signed as a solo artist — a departure that would make him one of the decade's biggest individual R&B stars.
metadata.storyHook: 1985. The group voted Bobby Brown out. Within a few years he was bigger as a solo act than the group he'd left.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified (moderate confidence — documentary source): Bobby Brown voted out of New Edition in 1985 over behavior issues, then went solo. Source: New Edition/NKOTB documentary https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bDPVXgPfIl4

sources.title: The Maurice Starr Story – YouTube (NE/NKOTB documentary)

questions.question: Which singer joined New Edition in 1987, replacing Bobby Brown and appearing on the group's 1988 album Heart Break?

metadata.fact: Johnny Gill joined New Edition in 1987, filling the gap left by Bobby Brown's departure two years earlier, and appeared on the group's 1988 album Heart Break.
metadata.storyHook: Two years after Bobby Brown left, Johnny Gill stepped in — and New Edition had a new sound on Heart Break.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Johnny Gill joined New Edition in 1987, appeared on Heart Break (1988). Source: Wikipedia (lineup history) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Edition

questions.question: Ready for the World, the Prince-tinged group behind 'Oh Sheila,' formed in which Michigan city in the early 1980s?

metadata.fact: Ready for the World formed in Flint, Michigan in the early 1980s — an unusual hometown, far from the coastal R&B hubs, for a group whose Prince-tinged sound would briefly dominate the charts.
metadata.storyHook: Flint, Michigan. Not Detroit, not Los Angeles. Ready for the World's #1 hit came out of a city most people wouldn't guess.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Ready for the World formed in Flint, Michigan. Source: Oh Sheila YouTube description (Ready For The World bio) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mvP1vdAeTpk

sources.title: Ready For The World – 'Oh Sheila' – YouTube description

questions.question: The Whispers recorded their 1970s-80s peak material, including 'Rock Steady,' for which label, also associated with Shalamar and the SOS Band?

metadata.fact: The Whispers recorded their 1970s-80s peak material, including 'Rock Steady,' for Solar Records (Sound of Los Angeles Records) — a label also associated with Shalamar and the SOS Band's run into the 1980s R&B mainstream.
metadata.storyHook: Solar Records. Same label ecosystem as Shalamar and the SOS Band — and the Whispers were right in the middle of it.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Whispers recorded for Solar Records, associated with Shalamar and SOS Band. Sources: Wikipedia (Rock Steady) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Steady_(The_Whispers_song), Wikipedia (Solar Records) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_Records

sources.title: Rock Steady – Wikipedia (label credit and context)

questions.question: Force MDs, who started as street performers on the Staten Island Ferry, formed in which New York City borough?

metadata.fact: Force MDs formed in Staten Island, New York City — originally performing as street singers on the Staten Island Ferry before becoming a recording act.
metadata.storyHook: Before the records, before Krush Groove, Force MDs were singing for tips on the Staten Island Ferry.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Force MDs from Staten Island, originally Staten Island Ferry street performers. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_MDs

questions.question: Force MDs' 'Tender Love' was featured in which 1985 film about the early hip-hop and R&B music business?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 2 OF 3 — THE 1985 FILM FEATURING 'TENDER LOVE'

metadata.fact: 'Tender Love' appeared in and on the soundtrack of Krush Groove (1985), a film dramatizing the early hip-hop and R&B music business — giving Force MDs additional exposure beyond radio.
metadata.storyHook: Krush Groove put the early rap and R&B business on screen — and Force MDs' 'Tender Love' was right there on the soundtrack.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Tender Love' featured in Krush Groove (1985). Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tender_Love

reserve.question: DeBarge, the family group behind 'Rhythm of the Night,' recorded primarily for which Motown subsidiary label?

metadata.fact: DeBarge recorded primarily for Gordy Records throughout their 1980s run — the same Motown subsidiary that also released the Mary Jane Girls' catalog.
metadata.storyHook: Gordy Records. Same Motown subsidiary, two completely different 1980s acts — DeBarge and the Mary Jane Girls.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: DeBarge recorded primarily for Motown's Gordy Records imprint. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeBarge

reserve.question: DeBarge's 'Rhythm of the Night' gained extra exposure through its prominent placement in which martial-arts-themed 1985 film?

metadata.fact: 'Rhythm of the Night' gained additional exposure through its prominent placement in The Last Dragon (1985), helping push the single into mainstream pop territory.
metadata.storyHook: A martial-arts film and a DeBarge single, tied together in 1985 — and the song reached further into the pop charts because of it.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Rhythm of the Night' featured in The Last Dragon (1985). Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_of_the_Night_(song)

reserve.question: New Edition's debut single 'Candy Girl,' released July 19, 1983, came out on which independent Boston-based label?

metadata.fact: 'Candy Girl,' New Edition's debut album, was released July 19, 1983 on Streetwise Records — Maurice Starr's own independent Boston label — before the group moved to a major label for later releases.
metadata.storyHook: July 19, 1983. Streetwise Records — Maurice Starr's own label — put out New Edition's very first album.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Candy Girl' album released July 19, 1983 on Streetwise Records. Sources: Wikipedia (album) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candy_Girl_(album), Wikipedia (song) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candy_Girl_(New_Edition_song)

rounds.description: The archival pop-culture connections hiding inside this era's legacy.

questions.question: DeBarge's classic lineup of five siblings — Bunny, El, Mark, Randy, and James — included which member as the group's sole female voice?

metadata.fact: DeBarge's classic lineup consisted of five siblings — Bunny, El, Mark, Randy, and James — with Bunny DeBarge as the group's only sister among four brothers.
metadata.storyHook: Five DeBarge siblings. Four brothers, and one sister: Bunny.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: DeBarge's classic lineup was Bunny, El, Mark, Randy, and James DeBarge, with Bunny as the sole sister. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeBarge

questions.question: Cameo's 'Word Up!' was covered by Gun, a Scottish hard rock band, in 1994 — reaching the UK Top 10. Which act covered it?

metadata.fact: Cameo's 'Word Up!' was covered by Gun, a Scottish hard rock band, in 1994 — reaching the UK Top 10 and introducing the song to a new rock-oriented audience nearly a decade after the original.
metadata.storyHook: A Scottish hard rock band took 'Word Up!' into the UK Top 10 in 1994 — eight years after Cameo's original, in a completely different genre.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Word Up!' covered by Gun (Scottish hard rock band) in 1994, UK Top 10. Note: Korn also covered the song in 2004 with lower chart impact; this question specifically addresses the Gun version. Source: Wikipedia (cover versions section) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_Up!

questions.question: Maurice Starr, who created New Edition, applied a similar manufactured-group formula in 1984 to create which other hugely successful vocal group?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — MAURICE STARR'S OTHER CREATION

metadata.fact: Maurice Starr applied a similar manufactured-group formula in 1984 to create New Kids on the Block, aiming the same model at a different audience than New Edition — and NKOTB went on to sell millions of albums worldwide.
metadata.storyHook: Maurice Starr didn't stop at New Edition. The same blueprint, aimed at a different audience, became New Kids on the Block.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Maurice Starr formed New Kids on the Block in 1984 using a formula similar to New Edition's. Source: Genius artist bio https://genius.com/artists/Maurice-starr

reserve.question: The Whispers, who scored their biggest hit with 'Rock Steady' in 1987, actually formed around twins Walter and Wallace Scott over two decades earlier, in which year?

metadata.fact: The Whispers formed in 1963 in Los Angeles, built around twins Walter and Wallace Scott — making their 1987 commercial peak with 'Rock Steady' the product of an unusually long career arc by R&B standards.
metadata.storyHook: 1963. Twenty-four years before 'Rock Steady.' The Whispers had already been a group for nearly a quarter-century by the time they had their biggest hit.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Whispers formed in 1963 in Los Angeles around twins Walter and Wallace Scott. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Whispers

reserve.question: Force MDs' 'Tender Love' appeared on which 1985 album, the group's second studio release?

metadata.fact: 'Tender Love' appeared on Chillin' (1985), Force MDs' second studio album — the release that delivered their commercial breakthrough.
metadata.storyHook: 'Chillin'.' That's the album 'Tender Love' came from — Force MDs' second try, and the one that broke through.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Tender Love' was from Force MDs' second studio album, Chillin' (1985). Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tender_Love
